steps.name: CheckForFrontImage
steps.label: Check for Front Image
steps.goal: We need at least one image in the source directory that has the word "front" on it. It should also be 1024x1024
steps.pass_criteria: front image exists.
steps.fail_criteria: could not find a 1024 image with front in the name.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-build the structure to the studio's convention — when the convention is clear and the inputs are present.
steps.max_scenario: The convention is undocumented or inconsistent across artists; you rebuild and reconcile it by hand.

steps.name: CheckForTpose
steps.label: Check for T-Pose
steps.goal: Resolve the character's front T-pose — the starred keeper, else the newest tpose candidate on disk, else generate one grounded on the anchor. Stashed in shared_data as "t_pose" for GenerateModel.
steps.pass_criteria: a tpose image exists on disk and shared_data["t_pose"] points at it.

steps.name: EnsureHeadshot
steps.label: Ensure Headshot
steps.goal: Create a Headshot the same way we do on the character dashbord.
steps.pass_criteria: Headshot is created

steps.name: EnsureFacialExpressions
steps.label: Ensure Facial Expressions
steps.goal: If the facial expressions don't exist - we need to create them - using the same tooling we use to generate the 420p video of all the expressions from the head shot. After the video is created the app should attempt to guess the best frame for each expression. Source only: the artist may still be choosing/painting these over, so nothing is copied to render and the MSD is untouched - publishing what was chosen is PrepImages' job in the publish recipe.
steps.pass_criteria: Facial Expressions created

steps.name: GenerateModel
steps.label: Generate Model
steps.goal: Create a Model — from the T-pose for characters (ensured by CheckForTpose), from the front/main image for props and environments.
steps.pass_criteria: .glb file has been created in the renders folder
steps.fail_criteria: An error occurred in the creation of the model.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-build the structure to the studio's convention — when the convention is clear and the inputs are present.
steps.max_scenario: The convention is undocumented or inconsistent across artists; you rebuild and reconcile it by hand.

steps.name: GenerateModelFromTpose
steps.label: Generate Model From Tpose
steps.goal: Generate a meshy model from shared_data tpose if it exists.
steps.pass_criteria: model generated

steps.name: MoveImagesToRender
steps.label: Move Images to Render
steps.goal: Move any of the images, glb files, or video from the source directory into the render directory of the current pathObject. register them in the msd.
steps.pass_criteria: Media is moved

steps.name: CreateMovPreview
steps.label: Create mov preview
steps.goal: take all the images/videos in the render directory and create a video of them - each image should get 1 second of playback time in the video.
steps.pass_criteria: video created

steps.name: BuildPlaylist
steps.label: Build Playlist
steps.goal: Build a playlist of every image, glb, or video within the render folder.
steps.pass_criteria: Design Playlist exists with all the review media in it.

steps.name: SubmitReview
steps.label: Submit Review
steps.goal: Submit the review mp4 file for review in alchemy
steps.pass_criteria: review created

steps.name: AddToDailiesPlaylist
steps.label: Add to dailies playlist
steps.goal: Add the mp4 review to the dailies playlist.  if the dailies playlist doesn't exist, create it.
steps.pass_criteria: review added to playlist

steps.name: EnsureHeight
steps.label: Ensure Height
steps.goal: Ensure that there is a set Height for this asset before moving forward - all scale calculations depend on this down the line.  Important to get right in the design phase.
steps.pass_criteria: Height is set.

steps.name: EnsureCharacterRigType
steps.label: Ensure Character Rig Type
steps.goal: if we're dealing with a chr (pathObject parent) we need to know that a Character type is set - humanoid for example, quadraped, bird, etc...
steps.pass_criteria: Character Type is set.

steps.name: CheckForSourceFiles
steps.label: Check For Source Files
steps.goal: Confirm the dsn task version has source files / has been started.
steps.pass_criteria: at least one source file is present.
steps.min_scenario: You eyeball the asset against the checklist by hand — naming, scale, topology, etc. — when it's clean and there's nothing to fix.
steps.max_scenario: You miss something (or there's a lot to fix); it ships, breaks in a downstream department, and bounces back days later for a re-publish.

steps.name: EnsureMainImage
steps.label: Ensure Main Image
steps.goal: Ensure the asset's DEFAULT-variant main image exists (the design that seeds the anchor and poses). Generate one from the asset + Style spine if the dashboard hasn't produced one yet.
steps.pass_criteria: a default main image exists and is recorded as the default keeper.
steps.fail_criteria: the asset can't be resolved or generation raises.
steps.min_scenario: A concept artist sketches a clean front design of the character / prop / location in one quick pass.
steps.max_scenario: It takes multiple rounds of drawing and revision to land an approvable front design for a complex or unfamiliar asset.

steps.name: EnsureAnchor
steps.label: Ensure Anchor
steps.goal: Ensure the asset has an anchor (reference_design) — the approved identity image that grounds every other generative task. Default it to the main image when one isn't chosen.
steps.pass_criteria: reference_design points at an existing image.
steps.fail_criteria: the asset can't be resolved or no main image exists to anchor on.
steps.min_scenario: You pick the approved front as the reference everyone grounds on — a single decision.
steps.max_scenario: Without a designated reference, downstream looks drift off-model and have to be re-reconciled later.

steps.name: EnsureCharPoses
steps.label: Ensure Char Poses
steps.goal: For characters, ensure the head_shot, front T-pose and back T-pose deliverables exist — each derived from the anchor (same person, same outfit, pose/framing only). Non-character assets skip this step.
steps.pass_criteria: all three character poses exist on disk (or the asset is not a character).
steps.fail_criteria: the asset can't be resolved or a pose generation raises.
steps.min_scenario: An artist redraws the approved character in a neutral headshot and front/back T-pose for modelling — quick when the design is simple and on-model.
steps.max_scenario: Keeping identity and costume consistent across head, front and back turnaround takes many careful passes for a detailed character.

steps.name: EnsureDesignModel
steps.label: Ensure Design Model
steps.goal: Checks for a .glb file in the source / render directory, copies it to the render directory if found in source.
steps.pass_criteria: glb file exists in the render directory

steps.name: PrepImages
steps.label: Prep Images
steps.goal: Copy the ensured deliverables (anchor + per-variant mains + character poses) from source to the render dir, then commit the dsn MSD data (anchor / head_shot / t_pose / t_pose_back / variant.{slug}.main; front T-pose = primary_view for characters).
steps.pass_criteria: the chosen deliverables are in the render dir and the MSD data is written.
steps.fail_criteria: the asset can't be resolved or no deliverables were found to publish.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-copy the approved images into the publish folder and note which is the model source — quick when you remember the convention.
steps.max_scenario: Files land in the wrong place or the wrong view is tagged as the model source, and a downstream department builds off the wrong image.

steps.name: ComposeExpressionSheet
steps.label: Compose Expression Sheet
steps.goal: Compose the character's expression sheet - the design plus every published expression as one wordless image - into the RENDER dir, from the items the MSD registered, then re-commit the MSD so the sheet is recorded.
steps.pass_criteria: the sheet is composed in render and recorded on the MSD, or the character has no expressions yet.
steps.fail_criteria: expressions are registered but the sheet could not be written.
steps.min_scenario: You hand-copy the approved images into the publish folder and note which is the model source — quick when you remember the convention.
steps.max_scenario: Files land in the wrong place or the wrong view is tagged as the model source, and a downstream department builds off the wrong image.

steps.name: CreateThumbnails
steps.label: Create Thumbnails
steps.goal: Create the version / task / asset thumbnails from the best design image (headshot, else main) before publishing, so the version thumb travels with the publish and the asset/task thumbs are ready for the grid.
steps.pass_criteria: version, task and asset thumbnails are written.
steps.fail_criteria: no design image to thumbnail, or thumb creation raises.
steps.min_scenario: You crop a representative thumbnail by hand and drop it in the right place — quick when you remember the convention.
steps.max_scenario: Thumbnails get forgotten or land in the wrong place, so browse views show blank cards and nobody can tell assets apart at a glance.

steps.name: Publish
steps.label: Publish
steps.goal: Publish the Design — copy the version to publish/latest and re-commit the MSD on the published object.
steps.pass_criteria: publish is complete.
steps.min_scenario: You manually copy the version to the publish/latest location and a coordinator hand-updates the tracker and pings downstream — when everyone actually does their part.
steps.max_scenario: The coordinator's slammed and forgets (or no one notifies downstream); everyone waiting burns days on Slack, text, email, phone, and walking the building to find out if it's ready.

steps.name: PopulateProfileImages
steps.label: Populate Profile Images
steps.goal: After publishing this design, refresh the crew documents so every published asset's reference imagery — the anchor for all assets, plus the headshot for characters — is embedded inline under its profile.
steps.pass_criteria: character_profiles.md / location_profiles.md carry the published assets' reference images and their PDFs are regenerated.
steps.fail_criteria: the population raises before any document is updated.
steps.min_scenario: You paste the approved character / location art into the production bible by hand — quick for one asset.
steps.max_scenario: Across a full cast and set list it's a tedious manual layout pass that goes stale the moment a design is re-approved.

steps.name: Height
steps.label: Height
steps.goal: We may need a different Button Kind of "widget" for this.   I essentially want a way to see/edit the height of the character here since it's so central to everything after the design publish.
steps.pass_criteria: height is set on the character registry

steps.name: DesignSlots
steps.label: Design Slots
steps.goal: Slots for each design deliverable, filled by dragging a file from Source Files. The tag becomes a pointer on the asset instead of something inferred from the filename, and the T-pose slot shows what Generate Model will build the mesh from.
steps.pass_criteria: each deliverable shows the image the build recipe will use
steps.fail_criteria: a slot resolves to something other than what the recipe picks.

steps.name: RigPublishQuick
steps.label: Rig Publish Quick
steps.goal: This will publish the current design - publish the resulting model, and publish the rig after that.  We'll follow the pattern we use in our "process designs" button but we'll only be running the build and publish phases on the model and rig pipelines to keep the focus on speed.
steps.pass_criteria: Successfully published a rig for this character

steps.name: BuildUeRig
steps.label: Build UE Rig
steps.goal: This button will:  Ensure a design publish (run one if it hasn't yet been published) Ensure a model publish, Ensure an "Assets" location for unreal in the current project, Run a UE rig build in that location, Run a UE render in that location.
steps.pass_criteria: A turntable of the rigged design coming out of UE
